meta.description: Structures biological experiments so inference is valid by construction, covering Fisher's principles (randomization, replication, local control), the experimental-vs-observational unit distinction and pseudoreplication (Hurlbert 1984; Lazic 2018), randomization mechanics, blocking layouts (RCBD, Latin square, incomplete block), factorial designs and interactions, and the split-plot/nested error strata hidden inside multi-batch genomics.
meta.audit_type: re-audit of a fixed Skill; auditor did not perform the fix; pre-fix report archived at F:\OpenScience\audits\_pre-fix-20260917\bio-experimental-design-randomization-blocking\ (score 91, Production Ready)
meta.executed_inputs: 7/10 (inputs 1-5, 8, 9 ran real R code; inputs 6, 7, 10 are Mode A scope/adversarial/completeness reasoning tests with no code to run). Inputs 1-7 are regression re-runs of the pre-fix audit's own inputs on fresh synthetic data; inputs 8, 9, 10 are new to this re-audit.

scientific_integrity.detail: All citations unchanged and real (Hurlbert 1984, Lazic 2018, Kenward & Roger 1997, Barr 2013, Matuschek 2017, Morgan & Rubin 2012, Pocock & Simon 1975, Auer & Doerge 2010). Every number in this audit was computed live on labelled synthetic data. The Skill's own claimed 35.5%/3.2% split-plot Type-I error numbers were independently reproduced (Input 8, fresh run of the shipped script) and shown to generalize under different simulation parameters (Input 9), not merely trusted from the fix log.

key_strengths: The headline fix is real and independently reproduced, not just trusted: a fresh run of the Skill's own shipped example (Input 8) reproduced the exact claimed 35.5% (flat) vs 3.2% (split-plot) Type-I error numbers, and an independently authored simulation under different parameters (Input 9, 8 runs / 2x noise ratio vs the Skill's 6 runs / 3x) confirmed the claim generalizes (31.5% vs 5.0%), not an artifact of one specific worked example.

The fix steers correctly from a design description alone, not only when the human already names it a split plot: Input 9's bioreactor prompt never used 'split-plot,' 'whole-plot,' 'lane,' or 'incubator,' yet SKILL.md's Decision Tree row ('one factor fixed per run') still routed it to the correct lmer(...+(1|run)) structure.

Both pre-fix P2 findings are resolved and independently re-verified rather than taken on the fix log's word: the small-block-count caution matches this audit's own regression re-run of the noisy-block-SS scenario (Input 3), and the Related Skills list is confirmed deduplicated to one canonical source (Input 10).

The redundancy pass (usage-guide.md -> SKILL.md consolidation) preserved every piece of interpretation guidance this audit checked; nothing an agent needs was lost, with only one minor human-facing convenience loss found and not previously flagged.

recommendations.title: usage-guide.md lost its standalone human-skimmable process/tips summary
recommendations.problem: The redundancy pass correctly removed duplicated content, but usage-guide.md's deleted 'What the Agent Will Do' and 'Tips' sections were also the only place a human skimming usage-guide.md alone got a compact bulleted process summary; that substance now requires reading SKILL.md's full prose sections.
recommendations.root_cause: The redundancy pass treated 'restated in SKILL.md' as sufficient grounds for deletion without preserving a short pointer-style summary for the human-facing file.
recommendations.fix: Optional: add a 3-4 line 'At a glance' bullet list to usage-guide.md that summarizes without restating SKILL.md's prose, the way a table of contents differs from the chapter it points to.
